Tomato___Bacterial_spot.label: Bacterial spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.evidence: Small dark, water-soaked lesions, often with yellow halos.
actions: Remove spotted leaves and avoid overhead watering.
Apply a copper-based bactericide; rotate crops next season.

Tomato___Early_blight.label: Early blight (Alternaria)
Tomato___Early_blight.evidence: Brown lesions with concentric target rings on older leaves.
actions: Prune the lower affected leaves and mulch to stop soil splash.
Apply a chlorothalonil or copper fungicide every 7-10 days.
Water at the base in the morning.

Tomato___Late_blight.label: Late blight (Phytophthora)
Tomato___Late_blight.evidence: Large greasy grey-green patches that spread fast in cool, wet weather.
actions: Remove and bag infected plants; do not compost.
Warn neighbours: late blight spreads by wind.
Protect healthy plants with a copper fungicide before rain.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.label: Leaf mold
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.evidence: Pale yellow spots on top, olive-green mould underneath.
actions: Increase airflow and lower humidity; space plants out.
Remove affected leaves; apply a fungicide if it spreads.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.label: Septoria leaf spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.evidence: Many small circular spots with dark borders and light centres.
actions: Strip infected lower leaves and mulch the soil.
Apply a fungicide every 7-10 days in wet weather.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.label: Two-spotted spider mites
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.evidence: Fine stippling and bronzing; webbing on leaf undersides.
actions: Hose leaf undersides with a strong water jet.
Apply insecticidal soap or neem oil every 5 days for two weeks.
Mites love hot, dry weather: keep plants well watered.

Tomato___Target_Spot.label: Target spot (Corynespora)
Tomato___Target_Spot.evidence: Brown lesions with light centres and concentric rings, on leaves and fruit.
actions: Remove infected leaves and improve airflow.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.label: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.evidence: Upward-curling, yellow-edged, stunted leaves; spread by whiteflies.
actions: Remove infected plants; the virus is incurable.
Control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps and insect netting.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.label: Tomato mosaic virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.evidence: Light and dark green mottling, distorted fern-like leaves.
actions: Remove infected plants and disinfect tools and hands.

Tomato___healthy.label: Healthy tomato leaf
Tomato___healthy.evidence: No lesions, mottling or pest damage detected.
actions: Keep the current care routine and check again in two weeks.
